arxiv-2107-10764.title: Nonlinear transformation of complex amplitudes via quantum singular value transformation
arxiv-2107-10764.creator: Naixu Guo, Kosuke Mitarai, Keisuke Fujii
arxiv-2107-10764.description: Abstract Due to the linearity of quantum operations, it is not straightforward to implement nonlinear transformations on a quantum computer, making some practical tasks like a neural network hard to be achieved. In this work, we define a task called nonlinear transformation of complex amplitudes and provide an algorithm to achieve this task.

arxiv-2205-02267.title: Time Shifts to Reduce the Size of Reservoir Computers
arxiv-2205-02267.creator: Thomas L. Carroll, Joseph D. Hart
arxiv-2205-02267.description: Abstract A reservoir computer is a type of dynamical system arranged to do computation. Typically, a reservoir computer is constructed by connecting a large number of nonlinear nodes in a network that includes recurrent connections. In order to achieve accurate results, the reservoir usually contains hundreds to thousands of nodes.

arxiv-2210-06966.title: Conics on Barth–Bauer octics
arxiv-2210-06966.creator: Alex Degtyarev
arxiv-2210-06966.description: Abstract We analyze the configurations of conics and lines on a special class of Kummer octic surfaces. In particular, we bound the number of conics by 176 176 and show that there is a unique surface with 176 176 conics, all irreducible: it admits a faithful action of one of the Mukai groups.

arxiv-2302-04807.creator: Javier de Cruz Pérez 1,2,3 and Joan Solà Peracaula 2
arxiv-2302-04807.description: Abstract Extensions of the gravitational framework of Brans & Dicke (BD) are studied by considering two different scenarios: i) ‘BD- Λ \Lambda CDM’, in which a rigid cosmological constant, Λ \Lambda , is included, thus constituting a BD version of the vanilla concordance Λ \Lambda CDM model (the current standard model of cosmology with flat three-dimensional geometry), and ii) ‘BD-RVM’,

arxiv-2308-05510.title: Advancing space-Based gravitational wave astronomy: Rapid parameter estimation via normalizing flows
arxiv-2308-05510.creator: Minghui Du †, Bo Liang †, He Wang, Peng Xu, Ziren Luo, Yueliang Wu
arxiv-2308-05510.description: Abstract Gravitational wave (GW) astronomy is witnessing a transformative shift from terrestrial to space-based detection, with missions like Taiji at the forefront. While the transition brings unprecedented opportunities for exploring massive black hole binaries (MBHBs), it also imposes complex challenges in data analysis, particularly in parameter estimation amidst confusion noise.

arxiv-2309-12678.title: QAL-BP: An Augmented Lagrangian Quantum Approach for Bin Packing
arxiv-2309-12678.creator: Lorenzo Cellini, Antonio Macaluso, Michele Lombardi
arxiv-2309-12678.description: Abstract The bin packing is a well-known NP-Hard problem in the domain of artificial intelligence, posing significant challenges in finding efficient solutions. Conversely, recent advancements in quantum technologies have shown promising potential for achieving substantial computational speedup, particularly in certain problem classes, such as combinatorial optimization.

arxiv-2311-08111.title: Solving Time-Dependent Traveling Salesman Problem with Time Windows under Generic Time-Dependent Travel Cost
arxiv-2311-08111.creator: Duc Minh Vu, Mike Hewitt, Duc Duy Vu
arxiv-2311-08111.description: Abstract In this paper, we present formulations and an exact method to solve the Time Dependent Traveling Salesman Problem with Time Window (TD-TSPTW) under a generic travel cost function where waiting is allowed. A particular case in which the travel cost is a non-decreasing function has been addressed recently.

arxiv-2412-05725.title: Black Swan: Abductive and Defeasible Video Reasoning in Unpredictable Events
arxiv-2412-05725.creator: Aditya Chinchure Sahithya Ravi Raymond Ng Vered Shwartz, Boyang Li Leonid Sigal
arxiv-2412-05725.description: Abstract The commonsense reasoning capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs), especially in abductive reasoning and defeasible reasoning, remain poorly understood. Most benchmarks focus on typical visual scenarios [ 1 , 42 , 23 ] , making it difficult to discern whether model performance stems from keen perception and reasoning skills, or reliance on pure statistical recall.

arxiv-2502-13294.title: The “Who”, “What”, and “How” of Responsible AI Governance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of (Actor, Stage)-Specific Tools
arxiv-2502-13294.creator: Blaine Kuehnert, Rachel M. Kim, Jodi Forlizzi, Hoda Heidari
arxiv-2502-13294.description: Abstract . The implementation of responsible AI in an organization is inherently complex due to the involvement of multiple stakeholders, each with their unique set of goals and responsibilities across the entire AI lifecycle. These responsibilities are often ambiguously defined and assigned, leading to confusion, miscommunication, and inefficiencies.

pmc-11621475.creator: Young-Min Ye
pmc-11621475.description: established.2 Commonly reported AEFIs include cutaneous reactions, such as delayed urticaria, maculopapular rashes, or nonspecific eruptions. Local reactions are the most frequent AEFIs. Urticaria, the most common manifestation of anaphylaxis−a potentially life-threatening reaction−requires immediate diagnosis and management. Vaccine safety studies focus on monitoring urticaria that occurs immediately after vaccination.

pmc-11670284.title: Population genetics of the freshwater red alga Batrachospermum gelatinosum (Rhodophyta) II: Phylogeographic analyses reveal spatial genetic structure among and within five major drainage basins in eastern North America
pmc-11670284.creator: Roseanna M Crowell, Sarah J Shainker‐Connelly, Stacy A Krueger‐Hadfield, Morgan L Vis
pmc-11670284.description: The freshwater red alga Batrachospermum gelatinosum has a well‐documented distribution spanning historically glaciated and unglaciated eastern North America. This alga has no known desiccation‐resistant propagule; thus, long‐distance dispersal events are likely rare. We predicted strong genetic structure among drainage basins and admixture among sites within basins.

pmc-11689297.title: GENDER AND RACE AS MODERATORS BETWEEN ACTIGRAPHY SLEEP AND INFLAMMATORY MARKERS
pmc-11689297.creator: Yuqi Shen, Linying Ji, Claudette Kessler, Christopher Engeland, Orfeu Buxton, Alan Zonderman, Michele Evans, Alyssa Gamaldo
pmc-11689297.description: This cross-sectional study investigated gender and race differences in the association between actigraphic sleep (mean levels and variability) and inflammatory markers (circulating interleukin [IL]-6, IL-10, tumor necrosis factor [TNF]-𝛼 and C-reactive protein [CRP]). The study included participants from the HANDLSleep study (n=99; 74% female, 54% Black adults; age range: 46-82).

pmc-12531447.title: First Contact With Care Through Clinical Simulation in Nursing Students: Qualitative Study
pmc-12531447.creator: Eva García Carpintero-Blas, Pablo Del Pozo-Herce, Maria del Carmen Hernández-Cediel, Marta Rodríguez-García, Noelia Navas-Echazarreta, Elena Chover-Sierra, Antonio Martínez-Sabater, Raúl Juárez-Vela, Alberto Tovar-Reinoso
pmc-12531447.description: BackgroundClinical simulation with standardized patients provides nursing students with their first approach to care in a safe and realistic environment. This type of experience arouses intense emotions and supports the development of key competencies.ObjectiveThis study aimed to explore the perceptions of nursing students during their first contact with care through simulation experiences with standardized patients.

pmc-13091832.title: Endoscopic resection of lumbar intradural spinal tumors: A case series on feasibility, safety, and preliminary outcomes
pmc-13091832.creator: Facundo Van Isseldyk, Vincent Hagel
pmc-13091832.description: BackgroundIntradural spinal tumors are traditionally managed with open microsurgical approaches that provide effective tumor control but involve substantial soft tissue disruption. Although full endoscopic spine surgery is well established for degenerative pathology, its use for intradural tumors remains limited due to challenges related to dural opening, cerebrospinal fluid management, and intradural manipulation.

pmc-13200111.title: A feasibility study on a machine-learning-based quality assurance tool for spot-scanning proton therapy using delivery log files and treatment plans☆
pmc-13200111.creator: Sang Kyun Yoo, Sridhar Yaddanapudi, Bo Lu, Ethan Stolen, Siddhant Sen, Byongsu Choi, Jin Sung Kim, Keith Furutani, Chris Beltran, James J. Sohn
pmc-13200111.description: Graphical abstract Introduction Pencil beam scanning (PBS) has become the clinical standard in proton therapy due to its superior dose conformity [1], [2], [3]. The American Association of Physicists in Medicine (AAPM) Task Group (TG) 224 report emphasizes the critical importance of precision in proton therapy delivery, recommending specific tolerances for monitor units (MU) delivery and spot position [4].

pmc-13386558.title: The Iranian version of Betts’ questionnaire upon mental imagery: translation and confirmatory factor analysis
pmc-13386558.creator: Maryam Khalaji, Mahya Mohamadtaghi, Sahar Mohammadzadeh, Mahin Aghdaei, Alfredo Campos, Mert Kurnaz, Mustafa Altınkök
pmc-13386558.description: ObjectivesMental imagery plays a crucial role in cognitive and motor functioning. The present study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and psychometrically evaluate the Persian version of Sheehan's shortened form of Betts’ Questionnaire Upon Mental Imagery (QMI) among Iranian university students.

pmc-13400669.title: MRI features of ovarian metastases from appendiceal tumors and primary ovarian mucinous carcinoma: a comparative study
pmc-13400669.creator: Masaya Kawaguchi, Hiroki Kato, Tomotaka Kawamura, Takuya Naruse, Tatsuro Furui, Masanori Isobe, Natsuko Suzui, Tatsuhiko Miyazaki, Yoshifumi Noda, Abdelazim Elsayed Elhelaly, Hirohiko Imai, Masayuki Matsuo
pmc-13400669.description: ObjectiveTo identify the MRI characteristics of ovarian metastases from appendiceal tumors (OMAT) and compare them with the features of primary ovarian mucinous carcinoma (POMC).Materials and MethodsThis retrospective study included 49 patients with histopathologically confirmed, MRI-detectable, and unruptured OMAT (14 patients with 18 lesions) or POMC (35 patients with 36 lesions) who underwent preoperative MRI.
